title: A seed takes a trip
hook: An animal can connect two plants.

knows: Animals have structures and activities that can be studied.
doesNotKnow: The diagram follows a fruit from the parent plant to the bird, then a seed to a different location. Moving a viable seed away is seed dispersal. The particular scene is illustrative: the outcome of a real seed depends on the species and conditions.

misconception: The features shown in this question have only one possible interpretation.
objective: In the illustrated scenario, a hornbill eats a fruit and later drops a viable seed away from the parent plant. What has the bird done?

claims.text: An animal can connect two plants. In the illustrated scenario, a hornbill eats a fruit and later drops a viable seed away from the parent plant. What has the bird done? claims.text: An animal carries a seed and deposits it away from its parent plant. What is this movement called? Seed dispersal is the movement of seeds away from the parent plant; germination is later growth.
